status: post-opening depth decomposition frozen before endpoint readback
sample: same 4,236 adjacent-observed-year matched wet-dry route x RunNumber pairs; exact-consecutive-year sensitivity prespecified
question: When active-stop mean species richness rises with rainfall contrast, is that due to crossing from one to at least two species, or to additional species beyond the second within already multispecies stops?

exact_decomposition.coefficient_identity: OLS rain-contrast beta for delta mean richness must equal the sum of component betas under identical rows/covariates

primary_endpoints.name: delta_fraction_2plus_active
primary_endpoints.definition: wet minus dry fraction of active stops containing >=2 species
primary_endpoints.direction: estimate and CI; no directional gate because prior all-run decomposition was null

primary_endpoints.name: delta_excess_beyond_two_active
primary_endpoints.definition: wet minus dry sum(max(K-2,0)) / number of active stops

primary_endpoints.name: shared_active_stop_delta_species_mean
primary_endpoints.definition: within each matched pair, mean wet-minus-dry species count across StopNumbers active in both runs
primary_endpoints.role: local taxonomic deepening holding active-stop membership fixed

secondary_diagnostics: same-stop transition counts among shared-active stops: 1->1, 1->2, 1->3plus, 2plus->1, 2->2, 2->3plus, 3plus->lower, 3plus->same_or_higher
newly-active-stop mean species count in wet run
lost-active-stop mean species count in dry run

models.formula: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber)

interpretation_boundary.active_stop: acoustic detection, not occupancy or abundance
